q: What is a carbon credit offtake or forward purchase agreement, and what should I watch for before signing?
title: Carbon credit offtake agreements
short: An offtake or forward purchase agreement is a contract to sell carbon credits that do not exist yet, at an agreed price or formula, when they are issued. It can give a project early cash or a sure buyer. Before signing, check delivery obligations, shortfall penalties, credit specification, price terms and who bears registry and rule-change risk.

ul: Spot sale: credits already issued are transferred now for payment now.
Forward sale: you promise future credits at a price fixed today, or a floor with upside sharing, paid on delivery.
Prepaid forward: the buyer pays part upfront to fund the project, and you repay in credits or cash.
p: The International Emissions Trading Association (IETA) publishes model emission reduction purchase agreements (ERPAs) that many buyers start from.

ul: Delivery: firm volume or best efforts. A firm promise makes you liable if the project under-delivers.
Shortfall remedies: replacement credits, refund of prepayment, or damages based on market replacement cost.
Credit specification: registry, methodology, vintage, any quality label, and whether a corresponding adjustment is needed.
Price: fixed, floor, or index linked, and in which currency.
Costs: who pays verification and issuance levies.
Change in law: what happens if Indian rules on credit export or authorisation change.
Exclusivity and term: whether you can sell surplus credits to others, and how either side can exit.

p: Sign a firm forward only for volumes you are confident of, after at least one verified monitoring period if possible. Offer the rest on a best-efforts or right-of-first-refusal basis. If you take a prepayment, make sure the repayment terms do not threaten the business if the project fails.

These contracts move risk between buyer and seller in ways that are not obvious. Ask a lawyer who has handled carbon contracts to review title, tax and governing law, and check that you actually own the right to claim the reductions.

example.title: Illustration: what a shortfall clause can cost
lines: Firm forward: 3,000 credits a year at USD 8 (illustrative price)
Credits issued this year: 2,100, so the shortfall is 900
Replacement cost clause, market price USD 11: 900 x (11 minus 8) = USD 2,700 owed to the buyer
example.note: Prices are illustrative, not market data.
